eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the Wuhan Meteorological Bureau indicate a daily maximum of 27–28°C on September 1 under the influence of a residual tropical cyclone vortex and trough, which advected cooler northerly air and triggered scattered showers that limited solar heating. Real-time observations through midday showed temperatures peaking near 28°C amid overcast skies and northerly winds of 3–5 Beaufort, consistent with model consensus from regional numerical guidance. This strong alignment of surface data and agency outlooks underpins the near-certain market-implied probability for 28°C. A late-afternoon convective cell or station-specific microclimate reading could still shift the official high by 1°C, though such deviations appear unlikely given persistent cloud cover and the short remaining diurnal window.

Updated model runs or real-time measurements closer to resolution could still shift the exact recorded maximum within the narrow 24–26°C envelope.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current conditions and model consensus point to a daily maximum near 21°C in São Paulo on September 1, 2026, aligning with the market's strong preference (65.5% implied probability) for that outcome.** Persistent cloud cover, widespread rain and thunderstorms, and moderate northwest winds have limited daytime heating, with afternoon readings hovering around 19–20°C at major stations such as Congonhas and Guarulhos. High humidity (near 80–90%) and falling pressure further suppress temperature rises, consistent with a passing frontal system.

September climatology features average highs of 24–26°C, but today's setup deviates notably due to the active weather pattern. Forecast models show limited warming potential through the remainder of the day, keeping the probability of reaching 22°C modest (23% implied) and higher thresholds (23°C+) near zero. Official monitoring from Brazilian meteorological services reinforces this range, with no indications of rapid clearing that could allow stronger insolation.

Traders are weighting real-time observations and short-range guidance heavily, as resolution hinges on the verified daily maximum from standard stations. Any late-day clearing could nudge readings toward 22°C, but current evidence favors the 21°C bin as the most likely outcome.

eventMetadata.context_description:
Persistent monsoon-driven cloud cover and scattered showers are the dominant factors capping Lucknow’s maximum temperature on September 2, keeping trader-implied odds tightly clustered around 30–31 °C. Official IMD guidance and multiple model runs forecast generally overcast skies with spells of rain or thundershowers, which sharply reduce surface insolation and limit daytime warming despite the season’s typical climatological peak near 32–33 °C. High relative humidity (near 85–90 %) and light easterly winds further suppress sensible heating by enhancing evaporative cooling and maintaining a moist boundary layer. Recent heavy rainfall across Uttar Pradesh has already erased the seasonal deficit and reinforced this pattern, with yesterday’s observed maximum falling several degrees below normal. 

Model consensus is tight on the 29–31 °C envelope; any brief clearing could push readings toward the upper end of that range, while prolonged or heavier precipitation would favor the lower side. The market’s near-even split between 30 °C and 31 °C therefore reflects the narrow but real uncertainty in exact cloud breaks and rainfall timing within the next 24 hours.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Kuala Lumpur Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 2 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=wmkk

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Recent model runs show limited spread, supporting trader consensus on 34°C while assigning lower odds (18.5%) to 33°C if stronger storms arrive earlier. eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon flow over Luzon, reinforced by a distant tropical depression, continues to drive widespread cloud cover, scattered thunderstorms, and moderate to heavy rainfall across Metro Manila on September 2. Official PAGASA guidance and ensemble model runs indicate daytime maxima near 29–30 °C under these conditions, as thick cloud decks and frequent precipitation limit surface heating despite typical early-September insolation. Historical climatology for the first week of September shows similar monsoon-suppressed peaks around 30 °C. Traders appear to price modest upside uncertainty from potential breaks in cloud cover or localized heating into the 31–32 °C outcomes, while the 30 °C bin remains a close alternative if rainfall persists through peak heating hours. Updated PAGASA and global model guidance issued overnight will provide the next key data point for resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent marine layer depth and an approaching Pacific trough are suppressing daytime heating in the San Francisco Bay Area, with National Weather Service guidance pointing to highs in the mid-60s to low 70s on September 2 amid southwest flow, cloud cover, and possible drizzle. This pattern aligns with seasonal norms near 70°F yet runs 5–15°F below average due to the unusually deep marine layer measured at over 3,000 feet. Trader consensus clusters on 70–73°F outcomes, reflecting uncertainty in afternoon clearing potential and microclimate variations across official stations, while lower bins price in stronger onshore cooling. Updated model runs and evening observations will refine landfall timing for any weak frontal moisture before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from multiple models, including Yr.no and Climatempo, indicate a high near 19–20°C for São Paulo on September 2 under partly cloudy skies with light southeast winds and minimal precipitation. A passing cold front and associated cloud cover from September 1 have suppressed daytime heating below the monthly climatological average of ~23°C, while building high pressure favors gradual clearing that could allow modest additional warming. Ensemble spreads in guidance create the tight clustering of market-implied odds around 19–21°C, with traders weighting the balance between lingering marine influence or southeasterly flow versus any afternoon sun that might push readings slightly higher. Updated model runs and official observations through the evening of September 1 will refine the exact maximum before market resolution.

Historical early-September averages near 29 °C provide context, yet current boundary-layer moisture and steering patterns support a modest rebound. Additional high-resolution model runs and official updates from monitoring agencies over the next 48 hours will likely refine these probabilities before resolution.

title: Highest temperature in Singapore on September 3?
description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Singapore Changi Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=wsss

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.
